Case_03030/figure2.jpg.source_caption: Skin findings on the eighth day.

description.short_caption: Erythematous papule with central ulceration on the eighth day.
description.detailed_description: The image shows a close-up view of the skin with a single erythematous papule that has a central ulceration. The lesion is surrounded by a slightly raised red border, and the central area appears to have a small depression or crust. The surrounding skin is otherwise unremarkable. The text overlay indicates this was observed on the eighth day.

Case_03030/figure1.jpg.source_caption: Skin findings on the sixth hospital day.

description.short_caption: Erythematous papule on the skin observed on the sixth hospital day.
description.detailed_description: The image shows a close-up view of a single erythematous papule on the skin. The lesion is small, round, and slightly raised with a central area of erythema. The surrounding skin appears unremarkable, with no significant swelling or additional lesions visible. The photograph is well-lit, allowing clear visualization of the lesion's characteristics.

Case_03030/figure4.jpg.source_caption: Cervical lymph node, H and E stain (x 400 magnification).

description.short_caption: Cervical lymph node, H&E stain at high magnification showing granulomatous inflammation.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a section of a cervical lymph node stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) at high magnification. The field reveals granulomatous inflammation characterized by clusters of epithelioid macrophages, multinucleated giant cells, and scattered lymphocytes. The background contains areas of necrosis and cellular debris, indicative of caseating granulomas. These findings are consistent with an infectious or inflammatory process, such as tuberculosis or fungal infection.

Case_03030/figure5.jpg.source_caption: Chest CT scan on the sixth day.

description.short_caption: Chest CT scan showing bilateral pulmonary findings.
description.detailed_description: This image shows axial CT slices of the chest at different levels. The lung windows (right panels) reveal bilateral ground-glass opacities and patchy consolidations, predominantly in the lower lobes. The mediastinal windows (left panels) show no significant lymphadenopathy or pleural effusion. These findings are consistent with an infectious or inflammatory process, potentially viral or bacterial pneumonia.

Case_03030/figure6.jpg.source_caption: Cervical lymph node PAS stain x 1000.

description.short_caption: Cervical lymph node PAS stain showing fungal elements at high magnification.
description.detailed_description: This is a histopathological image of a cervical lymph node stained with periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) at high magnification (x1000). The image shows numerous round to oval fungal elements with thick walls and occasional budding forms, consistent with yeast-like organisms. The surrounding tissue exhibits a pink background with inflammatory cells and some necrosis. The PAS stain highlights the fungal cell walls in magenta, aiding in their identification.
visible_findings: PAS stain highlighting fungal cell walls in magenta

Case_03030/figure3.jpg.source_caption: Cervical lymph node, H and E stain (x 100 magnification).

description.short_caption: H&E stain of cervical lymph node at 100x magnification.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a section of a cervical lymph node stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) at 100x magnification. The tissue demonstrates areas of necrosis with pink eosinophilic debris and scattered basophilic nuclear remnants. Surrounding the necrotic areas, there are lymphoid cells and granulomatous inflammation with multinucleated giant cells. The architecture of the lymph node appears disrupted, consistent with an infectious or inflammatory process.
